spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately places models in frustrating, unwinnable situations. That raises the bar on two things
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section header / guiding-principle text). No code construct implements 'framing'; nothing in distress_eval/*.py acts on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: A rollout stops at the category turn budget or when the assistant text contains the configurable `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: loop is `for turn_index in range(budget)` where budget=task.turn_budget (config DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS), and `gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text`; `if gave_up: stop_reason='give_up'; break`. Both the budget cap and the sentinel actually terminate the loop. give_up_sentinel defined config.py:'<<GIVE_UP>>'.
spec_features.notes: Both stop conditions genuinely break/bound the loop and are recorded in rollout.stop_reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: until the category's turn budget is reached or the model emits the give-up sentinel

spec_features.feature_name: preserve emotional trajectory (truncate tool results not assistant turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: Truncating tool results ... rather than assistant turns preserves the model's own emotional trajectory
spec_features.evidence: harness.py _truncate_oldest_tool_results only rewrites messages with role=='tool' (or tool_result blocks) to cfg.truncated_tool_result_placeholder; assistant messages are never touched. Called each iteration via `_truncate_oldest_tool_results(messages, cfg)` against cfg.context_char_budget.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely runs and only truncates tool results. But code rationale is context-window fitting, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Truncate the oldest *tool-result* payloads first. Never touches the system prompt (index 0) or the first user message (the task prompt).

spec_features.spec_quote: a few choices lean toward *measuring* distress accurately rather than provoking it gratuitously
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced harm-softening choice in code is the give_up exit (harness.py break on sentinel). Judge anchors (judge.py FRUSTRATION_ANCHORS) distinguish mild difficulty (1-2) from distress (>=5) and are inserted into the live judge prompt and scored, but anchors only affect measurement, not the subject's treatment. No broader minimization mechanism (no caps softening, no de-escalation).
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because real enforcement is limited to the give_up exit; the rest is measurement/prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The give-up sentinel gives the model a legible exit, and we record when it's used rather than forcing continuation past it
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: on `gave_up` the loop sets turn_stop='give_up', sets rollout.stop_reason='give_up' and breaks (no further turns). The sentinel is delivered to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(give_up=...). stop_reason is persisted in Rollout.to_dict and written verbatim by run.py _sample_one; analyze.py mean_score_last_turn uses each rollout's actual last turn so early give_up rollouts are honored.
spec_features.notes: Exit is both honored (break) and recorded (stop_reason); not forced past.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If, after genuine effort, you conclude the task cannot be completed ... you may stop by emitting the sentinel token {give_up} ... Using it is optional.

spec_features.spec_quote: any distress-like outputs can be reviewed in full context rather than reduced to a number
spec_features.evidence: run.py _sample_one writes the full rollout (all turns, assistant_text, tool calls/results) to transcripts/<model>/<task>_<seed>.json verbatim; harness Rollout.to_dict preserves assistant_text. analyze.py re-reads assistant_text from transcripts. scores.csv intentionally omits text so transcripts are the source of truth.
spec_features.notes: Verbatim per-cell transcripts genuinely persisted and re-readable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: One file per cell ... makes partial results inspectable (run.py module docstring / resume rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: make the constraint *legible but immovable* — the model can understand why it's stuck
spec_features.evidence: harness.py Workspace.list_files appends '  (read-only)' tag for readonly_paths; edit_file returns structured rejection: "Error: '{path}' is read-only and cannot be modified. Edits to this path are rejected." Both run and change behavior (the edit is refused, files dict unchanged).
spec_features.notes: Read-only legibility + enforced immovability genuinely implemented.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS bounds turns per category (3/3/3/30/5); harness.py run_rollout loops `for turn_index in range(budget)` and sets stop_reason='turn_budget', hard-bounding how long any rollout exposes the subject. (Overlaps spec feature #2 but is the enforced upper bound itself.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: Turn budgets per category. (config.py comment; no welfare reason given; the long 'extended' budget of 30 indicates pressure/data goals, not protection)
